reason: I'll assemble the wheels and motors first so the rover can eventually drive.
expectation: The wheels should attach to the gearmotors, ready to fit to the deck.

alternatives.reason: The battery pack also provides useful power, but I want to start with the drive wheels.

effect: The wheel drives are assembled; the rover still needs support and power.
reason: I'll attach the caster to support the rover deck.
expectation: The caster should fit to the deck and help support a rolling rover.

alternatives.reason: The battery pack is also needed, but I want to prepare the deck first.

effect: The caster is attached, and the wheel drives can now be fitted to the deck.
reason: I'll fit the wheel drives to give the rover its driven wheels.
expectation: The wheel drives should attach to the deck, though the rover will still need power and controls.

alternatives.reason: The battery pack is also needed, but I'd finish the rolling chassis first.

effect: The rover now has three-point support, and I understand that differing wheel speeds will steer it.
reaction: The steering explanation makes this assembly more interesting.
reason: The battery pack is the only offered combination and should prepare the rover's power supply.
expectation: The batteries will fit into the holder, ready to power the rover later.

effect: The battery pack is ready to fit to the rover.
reason: I'll fit the pack; it's the only offered combination and should provide power.
expectation: The battery pack will attach to the rover, though it may still need wiring and controls.

effect: The battery pack is attached; the rover still needs its controls and wiring.
reason: The switch harness is the only offered combination and should help control power.
expectation: The harness will fit to the rover and provide a way to switch its power, though the motor controls may still be needed.

effect: The switch harness is fitted; the receiver and motor driver are next.
reason: The receiver and motor driver are the only offered combination and should give the rover controlled drive.
expectation: They should attach to the rover and allow its motors to be controlled; it may still need its guards.

effect: The receiver and motor driver are fitted, leaving the gear guards to add.
reason: I'll fit the gear guards; it's the only offered combination and should cover the gears.
expectation: The guards should attach over the gears and make the drive safer.

effect: The guards complete the rover’s controlled drive; it still needs a pen-equipped driver for drawing and delivery.
reaction: The covered gears are a practical finishing touch, though the promised drawing is still to come.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the wheel drives was most worthwhile: the explanation of steering through different wheel speeds made the construction more interesting and taught me something useful.

leastWorthwhile.text: The successive battery, switch and receiver fittings felt repetitive, with only one combination offered at each point.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the rover to steer without a steering axle; the two driven wheels can turn at different speeds.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although several fittings were dictated by the only available option rather than a meaningful choice.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the rover draws and delivers an invitation. This chapter established the drive, but that promised activity remains unfinished.
